size.$description: Sizes that differ by platform: the input decides them, since touch needs larger targets than a pointer (decisions/0010, chapter 06). Every platform's file names the same tokens with the same descriptions; only the values differ.

s.$description: The height of a control at size s: 24 on macOS, 28 on iOS and iPadOS, 32 on watchOS. It is below the recommended target on every platform, so its hit area stays size.target.minimum, except where a contract records otherwise (chapter 08).

use: control in a toolbar or a table row
dev.westron.usage.avoid: The default size: use size.control.m. A row's height: rows have heights of their own.

m.$description: The height of a control at the default size m: a button, a field, a segmented control. 32 on macOS, westron's control (decisions/0013); 36 on iOS and iPadOS, beside the system's own 34 (decisions/0013, revision of 2026-11-20); 44 on watchOS. A hit area takes size.target.minimum, not this height.

dev.westron.usage.avoid: A row's height: rows have heights of their own. A fixed height where text can grow: the height is a minimum. A hit area: use size.target.minimum.

l.$description: The height of a control at size l: the one prominent action of a form, a sheet or an empty state. 40 on macOS, 50 on iOS and iPadOS, 52 on watchOS.

dev.westron.usage.avoid: Every control on a screen: the large size marks the one action that leads.

minimum.$description: The least side of the area that takes a touch or a click on a control, whatever the control draws: 44 on iOS, iPadOS and watchOS, the recommended touch target; 28 on macOS, the recommended target for a pointer (chapter 08). A contract may record a control whose hit area is smaller, as Button's size s on macOS.

dev.westron.usage.avoid: A drawn size: use size.control.*. A row's height: rows have heights of their own.
